rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is consistently titled Surat al-Fajr without an initial waw in Qurans, tafsirs, and hadith books.
rows.anchor: لم يختلف في تسمية هذه السورة { سورة الفجر } بدون الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is Meccan by agreement, except for a report by Ibn Atiyya from Abu Amr al-Dani that some scholars considered it Medinan.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية باتفاق سوى ما حكى ابن عطية عن أبي عمرو الداني أنه حكى عن بعض العلماء وأنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was the tenth surah revealed, after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت العاشرة في عداد نزول السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse counts differ by regional tradition: Medina and Mecca count 32, Kufa and Syria 30, and Basra 29, with different verse endings assigned to نعمه, رزقه, بجهنم, and في عبادي.
rows.anchor: وعدد آيها اثنتان وثلاثون عند أهل العدد بالمدينة ومكة عدوا قوله { ونعمه } منتهى آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns Meccan polytheists through the examples of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh's people, promises the Prophet his enemies' decline, and warns of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ضرب المثل لمشركي أهل مكة في إعراضهم عن قبول رسالة ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It refutes the prosperous polytheists' belief that wealth means divine honor and believers' poverty means humiliation: they failed to share, grew greedier, and will regret not preparing through faith and good works.
rows.anchor: إبطال غرور المشركين من أهل مكة إذ يحسبون أن ما هم فيه من النعيم علامة على أن الله أكرمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths invoke times that display God's craftsmanship and power, especially dawn's transition from night to day and fully dark night, as well as times of worship such as the ten, even, and odd nights.
rows.anchor: القسم بهذه الأزمان من حيث إن بعضها دلائل بديع صنع الله وسعة قدرته فيما أوجد من نظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath confirms the assertion: an oath calls God to witness the statement, and God's oaths serve confirmation alone.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا القسم تحقيق المقسم عليه لأن القسم في الكلام من طرق تأكيد الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is directed to the Prophet, as the later references to God's acts toward Ad and God's watchfulness indicate; the oath indirectly assures deniers that its assertion will occur.
rows.anchor: كما دل عليه قوله :  { ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended oath builds anticipation for the assertion that follows.
rows.anchor: والمقصد من تطويل القسم بأشياء ،  التشويق إلى المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr is the first dawn light at the eastern horizon, the initial solar ray that pushes back darkness before illuminating the horizon and preceding sunrise; it is a striking sign of divine power and artistry.
rows.anchor: فالفجر ابتداء ظهور النور بعد ما تأخذ ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is blessed because it ends sleep, likened to death, and people regain awareness and turn to their familiar useful work.
rows.anchor: وهو وقت مبارك للناس إذ عنده تنتهي الحالة الداعية إلى النوم الذي هو شبيه الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-fajr is generic, the reading that best suits its coordination with the night in verse 4.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس وهو الأظهر لمناسبة عطف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One reported specific referent for al-fajr is the daily dawn prayer time.
rows.anchor: فقيل أريد وقت صلاة الصبح من كل يوم وهو عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة
rows.claim: Another reported referent is the dawn of the Sacrifice day, when pilgrims are at Muzdalifa; on this reading the article is definite by prior reference.
rows.anchor: فجر يوم النحر وهو الفجر الذي يكون فيه الحجيج بالمزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is coordinated with the ten nights as a general after a specific, or with dawn because the two oppose each other; it is an oath because night displays God's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: عطف الأعم على الأخص أو عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasri means to move through darkness: much of the night has elapsed, figuratively likened to a traveler's nocturnal journey.
rows.anchor: تقضي الليل في ظلامه بسير السائر في الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is compared with night retreating or becoming still and dark in other passages.
rows.anchor: تقضي الليل في ظلامه بسير السائر في الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause marks the settled darkness, when people have slept enough to perform night vigil.
rows.anchor: لأنه وقت تمكن ظلمة الليل فحينئذ يكون الناس أخذوا حظهم من النوم فاستطاعوا التهجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Abu Ja'far, and Yaqub read the final ya in connected recitation but omit it at a pause to preserve the rhyme endings.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب :  { إذا يسري } بياء بعد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic verse endings function like prose assonance and receive treatment like poetic rhyme; Abu Ali says deletion at a pause is no worse than retention, while outside a rhyme retention is better.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي :  وليس إثبات الياء في الوقف بأحسن من الحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub are also said to retain the ya both in connection and at a pause, following the underlying form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب بثبوت الياء بعد الراء في الوصل وفي الوقف على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers omit the ya in both positions, matching the Quranic codex spelling; readers who retain it follow transmitted recitation and treat the spelling as a pause form or as canonical practice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بدون ياء وصلا ووقفا ، وهذه الرواية يوافقها رسم المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex spelling does not weaken Nafi, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja'far's connected-reading tradition because Quranic spelling often reflects pausal pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وأما نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر فلا يوهن رسم المصحف روايتهم لأن رسم المصحف جاء على مراعاة حال الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tala means following: moonlight follows sunlight after sunset, figuratively, and the moon follows the sun through its phases; at the full moon its following is literal around sunset.
rows.anchor: التبع وأريد به خلف ضوئه في الليل ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crescent appears after sunset for three nights; near its first visibility and at full moon it follows the sun, and it illuminates many nights as a substitute for sunlight.
rows.anchor: فالهلال يظهر للناظرين عقب غروب الشمس ثم يبقى كذلك ثلاث ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to the moon's following highlights its visible manifestation, making the oath one by the moon and by the time it follows the sun, like the duha oath.
rows.anchor: لأن تلوه للشمس حينئذ تظهر منه مظاهر التلو للناظرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals that moonlight is borrowed from sunlight striking the moon's earth-facing surface, rather than being intrinsic; Ibn Ashur calls this a scientific miracle noted in his tenth introduction.
rows.anchor: وهذا إعجاز علمي من إعجاز القرآن وهو مما أشرت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order symbolizes Islam: the sun's guidance leaves no path for error and promises worldwide spread, while the moon shining in darkness resembles Islam's first appearance amid polytheism.
rows.anchor: وابتدىء بالشمس لمناسبة المقام إيماء للتنويه بالإسلام لأن هديه كنور الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day and night then represent Islam's clarity after polytheist error, opposite the order in Surat al-Layl; sky, earth, and finally the human soul follow as signs of guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر النهار والليل معه لأنهما مثل لوضوح الإسلام بعد ضلالة الشرك وذلك عكس ما في سورة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in jallaha most naturally refers to the sun: the day makes the sun appear, with manifestation figuratively attributed to the day; the oath is by day as evidence of the earth's precise order.
rows.anchor: ظاهره أنه عائد إلى الشمس فمعنى تجلية النهار بالشمس وقت ظهور الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun to refer to earth: daylight illuminates and unveils the earth to observers, as people say rain was sent when they mean the sky sent its water.
rows.anchor: أي أضاء الأرض فتجلت للناظرين لظهور المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the oath to the time of manifestation incorporates a reminder of divine favor.
rows.anchor: وقيد القسم بالنهار بقيد وقت التجلية إدماجا للمنة في القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and its direct and reflected lights symbolize faith emerging after disbelief and piety after sin, since darkness represents sin and light represents faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: ولما في حالها وحال أضوائها من الإيماء إلى أنها مثل لظهور الإيمان بعد الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night follows day in the oath because it is the opposing period of darkness.
rows.anchor: وأعقب القسم بالنهار بالقسم بالليل لأن الليل مقابل وقت النهار فهو وقت الإظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called Surat al-Layl in most Qurans and some tafsirs, Surat wa-l-Layl in most tafsirs, and al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi title it Surat wa-l-Layl idha yaghsha.
rows.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في معظم المصاحف وبعض كتب التفسير سورة الليل بدون واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities call it Meccan; Ibn Atiyya reports al-Mahdawi's view that it is Medinan or partly Medinan, linked to a reported occasion for verse 5 involving Abu al-Dahdah buying a palm from a hypocrite for orphans.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن عطية عن المهدوي أنه قيل :  إنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was the ninth surah revealed, after al-A'la and before al-Fajr, and has twenty verses.
rows.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى وقبل سورة الفجر .  وعدد آيها عشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah contrasts believers' honored virtues and reward with polytheists' faults and recompense, and says God guides people to good, rewarding guidance in both lives and the astray oppositely.
rows.anchor: احتوت على بيان شرف المؤمنين وفضائل أعمالهم ومذمة المشركين ومساويهم وجزاء كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger was sent to remind people of God and His reward; the fearful benefit, while the wretched turn away and face the great fire because they prefer worldly life.
rows.anchor: وأنه أرسل رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للتذكير بالله وما عنده فينتفع من يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse also embeds signs of God's power and fine workmanship.
rows.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك الإشارة إلى دلائل قدرة الله تعالى وبديع صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath continues the style of the preceding two surahs and confirms its assertion; night and day suit the contrast between good and evil striving, light and darkness, and beneficial or harmful outcomes.
rows.anchor: افتتاح الكلام بالقسم جار على أسلوب السورتين قبل هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day invite reflection on the ordered cosmos: night is especially marked by enveloping the earth and its creatures in darkness, while day reveals them; this was explained in the preceding Surat al-Shams.
rows.anchor: وخص بالذكر ما في الليل من الدلالة من حالة غشيانه الجانب الذي يغشاه من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their contrast suits the surah's subject: the different worldly and afterlife conditions of believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: واختير القسم بالليل والنهار لمناسبته للمقام لأن غرض السورة بيان البون بين حال المؤمنين والكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with night reverses Surat al-Shams because al-Layl was revealed earlier, when disbelief dominated and Islam was beginning to emerge, like night followed by day.
rows.anchor: وابتدىء في هذه السورة بذكر الليل ثم ذكر النهار عكس ما في سورة الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad statement that human striving differs creates suspense before its elaboration into the contrasting cases beginning with the one who gives.
rows.anchor: إجمال يفيد التشويق إلى تفصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of yaghsha is omitted, making the verb effectively intransitive because the lesson concerns everything covered by its darkness.
rows.anchor: لتنزيل الفعل منزلة اللازم لأن العبرة بغشيانه كل ما تغشاه ظلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing tajalli to daytime praises its brightness, which everyone can perceive, including the blind.
rows.anchor: وأسند إلى النهار التجلي مدحا له بالاستنارة التي يراها كل أحد ويحس بها حتى البصراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajalli means clarity, so the verse describes the clarity of daylight, as do the oaths by the sun's brightness and by morning light.
rows.anchor: والتجلي :  الوضوح ، وتجلي النهار :  وضوح ضيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording alludes to night darkness having prevailed before daylight followed it; darkness was the original state of the earth and solar system before God created and lit the sun, which explains dating days from nights.
rows.anchor: وأشير إلى أن ظلمة الليل كانت غالبة لضوء النهار وأن النهار يعقبها والظلمة هي أصل أحوال أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification of night and day by their temporal conditions follows the same explanation as the parallel wording in Surat al-Shams.
rows.anchor: والقول في تقييد الليل بالظرف وتقييد النهار بمثله

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: Alqama reports that he recited the night and day oaths followed by al-dhakar wa-l-untha; Abu al-Darda testified that he heard the Prophet recite this wording.
rows.anchor: عن علقمة قال :  « دخلت في نفر من أصحاب عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls it the Prophet's reading; Ibn Ashur explains that it reflects the early license to recite variant forms, later abrogated by the Prophet's final-life reading adopted by the canonical readers and written in Abu Bakr's codex.
rows.anchor: وسماها في « الكشاف » :  قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur refers readers to his sixth introduction for the meaning of the phrase the Prophet's reading.
rows.anchor: في المقدمة السادسة من مقدمات هذا التفسير معنى قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan and originally an adjective with an omitted feminine noun, potentially reward, victory, promise, or outcome.
rows.anchor: تأنيث الأحسن فهي بالأصالة صفة لموصوف مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify al-husna as Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقد يصير هذا الوصف علما بالغلبة فقيل :  الحسنى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify al-husna as the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: فقيل :  الحسنى الجنة ، وقيل :  كلمة الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify al-husna as prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل :  كلمة الشهادة ، وقيل :  الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify al-husna as almsgiving.
rows.anchor: وقيل :  الصلاة ، وقيل :  الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across these readings, affirming it means acknowledging its occurrence and implies wanting to attain it; the possibilities ultimately concern faith in God's promise of good reward, victory, or compensation.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجوه كلها فالتصديق بها الاعتراف بوقوعها ويكنى به عن الرغبة في تحصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in al-husna entails doing the deeds by which success is attained, and contrasts with the denial in verse 9.
rows.anchor: ويتضمن أنه يعمل الأعمال التي يحصل بها الفوز بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taysir makes something easy to obtain; its direct object is what is made easy, while the following li- phrase names the beneficiary, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: مفعول فعل التيسير هو الشيء الذي يجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusra means what is free of hardship, construed as the easy condition of afterlife bliss or as an easy rank or place; more broadly it covers anything beneficial and agreeable.
rows.anchor: الحالة التي لا تشق عليه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and Mujahid interpret al-yusra as Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرت اليسرى بالجنة عن زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-usra can mean the condition of hardship, namely punishment, or the place of hardship, namely Hell, as reinforced by the cited description of a hard day for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وإما مكانته وهي جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains facilitation as leading a person through the acts of felicity or misery; easy deeds are good because of their outcome, and difficult deeds are sins by their outcome.
rows.anchor: فالأعمال اليسرى هي الصالحة ، وصفت باليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Atiyya's interpretation, the feminine forms describe categories of deeds according to their consequences.
rows.anchor: فتأنيثهما باعتبار أن كلتيهما صفة طائفة من الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the future particle sa- signals continued facilitation from now through the end of life, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وحرف التنفيس على هذا التفسير يكون مرادا منه الاستمرار من الآن إلى آخر الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article on al-yusra and al-usra may be generic or referential, depending on the interpretation.
rows.anchor: لتعريف الجنس أو للعهد على اختلاف المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax seems reversed: the person is the direct object of facilitate while the easy or hard path is attached by li-, although the person does not benefit from ease in reaching either path.
rows.anchor: وهما لا ينتفعان بسهولة من أعلى أو من بخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One solution keeps facilitate literal and treats the construction as rhetorical inversion: the original sense is making the easy or hard path easy for the person, with inversion intensifying the facilitation.
rows.anchor: على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر بطريق القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inversion is compared with the Arabic expression about presenting a she-camel to a watering trough.
rows.anchor: على نحو ما وجهوا به قول العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second solution uses facilitate figuratively for preparation; li- is causal, and al-yusra and al-usra denote Paradise and Hell, with entry understood after the preposition.
rows.anchor: مستعملا مجازا مرسلا في التهيئة والإعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preparation interpretation, making entry quick is likened to making a difficult thing easy, since difficulty is associated with delay and ease with speed; the cited verse uses easy in the sense of quick.
rows.anchor: مشاكلة بنيت على استعارة تهكمية قرينتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same reading makes facilitation follow the acts already produced by giving, restraint, affirmation, or denial, and therefore concerns continuing those acts or increasing them.
rows.anchor: والتيسير مستقبل بعد حصولها فهو تيسير ما زاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility keeps facilitation literal without inversion: al-yusra and al-usra describe the corresponding conditions, and facilitation means persisting in the deed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى الآية :  أن يجعل التيسير على حقيقته

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ali reports that at a funeral in Baqi al-Gharqad the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether they should rely on that, he commanded them to work, since each person is eased toward the deeds for which they were created, then recited these verses.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال :   "  كنا مع رسول الله في بقيع الغرقد في جنازة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith's opening statement about each person's written destination is not the verse's subject: writing represents God's exact prior knowledge of what each person will do.
rows.anchor: معناه قد علم الله أن أحدا سيعمل بعمل أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about work is answered by treating righteous action as an indicator of a good end; mention of bad action completes the account rather than answering the question.
rows.anchor: أن فائدة العمل الصالح أنه عنوان على العاقبة الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to the Prophet's words because he recited it as explanation and evidence, especially the clause that God will facilitate; it shows that God enables people toward felicity or misery.
rows.anchor: فالذي يرتبط بالآية من اللفظ النبوي هو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse supports the command to work: deeds mark divine facilitation, with al-yusra signifying happiness and Paradise and al-usra misery and Hell.
rows.anchor: لأن الآية ذكرت عملا وذكرت تيسيرا لليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clauses describing those who give, are mindful, and affirm indicate that facilitation is caused by their deeds and rewards them by sustaining those deeds; al-yusra praises the deeds as divinely facilitated, as in al-A'la.
rows.anchor: وإذ كان الوعد بتيسير اليسرى لصاحب تلك الصلات الدالة على أعمال الإعطاء والتقوى والتصديق بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith distinguishes God's prior knowledge of human deeds from His address through religious law; deeds are signs of what God knew and means of reaching Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: وخلاصة الحديث أنه بيان للفرق بين تعلق علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving is named even though it is included in piety, and miserliness despite being included in self-sufficiency, to encourage Muslims to give; giving, piety, and faith mark Muslims, with their opposites marking polytheists.
rows.anchor: فالإعطاء والتقوى شعار المسلمين مع التصديق بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the rhetorical figures of combination with division and antithesis, with four paired oppositions: giving and stinginess, piety and self-sufficiency, affirmation and denial, and ease and hardship.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية محسن الجمع مع التقسيم ، ومحسن الطباق ، أربع مرات بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mughirat is the active participle of aghara, usually meaning to raid a people's home; attributing the raid to the horses is figurative because the riders raid and the horses are their means.
rows.anchor: والإغارة تطلق على غزو الجيش دارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighara can also mean rushing forward in travel.
rows.anchor: وتطلق الإغارة على الاندفاع في السير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan is a time adverb; if the referent is raiding cavalry, dawn is specified because they attacked after daybreak, as reflected in the warning cry and the cited verse.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا إذا غزوا لا يغيرون على القوم إلا بعد الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the referent is camels rushing from Muzdalifa to Mina on Sacrifice day, departing when the sun shone on Thabir, as in the saying addressed to the mountain.
rows.anchor: دفعها من مزدلفة إلى منى صباح يوم النحر وكانوا يدفعون بكرة

none: The segment contains only the verse text and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called Surat al-Asr in many Qurans, most tafsirs, and a fifth-century Kufic Qayrawani codex; some tafsirs and Sahih al-Bukhari title it Surat wa-l-Asr, following its first word.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تسميتها في مصاحف كثيرة وفي معظم كتب التفسير وكذلك هي في مصحف عتيق بالخط الكوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities consider it Meccan; Qatada, Mujahid, and Muqatil are reported to consider it Medinan.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة ومجاهد ومقاتل أنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was the thirteenth surah revealed, after al-Inshirah and before al-Adiyat; it has three verses and is among the shortest surahs, alongside al-Kawthar and al-Nasr.
rows.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الانشراح وقبل سورة العاديات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its aims include declaring the grave loss of disbelievers and those persisting in false practices after Islam's call reaches them, and the salvation of believers who do good and call others to truth.
rows.anchor: واشتملت على إثبات الخسران الشديد لأهل الشرك ومن كان مثلهم من أهل الكفر بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also establishes the virtue of patiently purifying oneself and inviting others to truth.
rows.anchor: وعلى فضيلة الصبر على تزكية النفس ودعوة الحق

rows.speaker: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن الحصين الأنصاري
rows.claim: The Tabi'i reports that two Companions would not part after meeting without one reciting Surat al-Asr to the other, then exchanging the customary farewell greeting; the departure greeting is Sunnah like the greeting on arrival.
rows.anchor: روى الطبراني بسنده إلى عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن الحصين الأنصاري

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says that if people reflected on this surah, it would suffice them; another reported wording says that if no other revelation had come, it would have sufficed.
rows.anchor: لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة لوسعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others are said to hold that the surah encompasses all the Quran's sciences, which the commentary will explain later.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره :  إنها شملت جميع علوم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by al-asr to confirm the report, as Quranic oaths generally do; the sworn time manifests God's creative artistry, power, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله تعالى بالعصر قسما يراد به تأكيد الخبر كما هو شأن أقسام القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever sense of al-asr is intended, it must denote a state that points to a divine act, established through an implied adjunct, contextual clue, or prior reference; as time it recalls God's power in creation and momentous blessings.
rows.anchor: وللعصر معان يتعين أن يكون المراد منها لا يعدو أن يكون حالة دالة على صفة من صفات الأفعال الربانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most familiar sense is the late-afternoon period, from when an object's shadow equals its noon shadow plus its length until it reaches twice its length beyond the noon shadow, around yellowing and the start of evening.
rows.anchor: وأشهر إطلاق لفظ العصر أنه علم بالغلبة لوقت ما بين آخر وقت الظهر وبين اصفرار الشمس

rows.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
rows.claim: Al-Harith ibn Hilliza's verse uses asran for the late-afternoon period approaching evening.
rows.anchor:
قال الحارث بن حِلزة :
آنستْ نبأة وأفزَعها القَنَّ *** اصُ عَصْراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Late afternoon recalls the nearing end of day, the sun and earth, Earth's orbit producing night and day, and changing atmospheric conditions, like the oaths by duha, night, day, and dawn.
rows.anchor: التي يتكون منها الليل والنهار كل يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is when people prepare to stop work in fields, gardens, and markets, recalling social order and God's inspiration of work rhythms; they return home to family, and the time is a blessing.
rows.anchor: وفيه يتحفز الناس للإقبال على بيوتهم لمبيتهم والتأنس بأهليهم وأولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day's decline also hints at human life nearing its end after youth, maturity, and old age; on the general-time reading, the article means every age.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى التذكير بمثل الحياة حين تدنو آجال الناس بعد مضي أطوار الشباب والاكتهال والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asr can mean the highly honored afternoon prayer, possibly the middle prayer in the cited verse; two hadith reports warn of missing it and of swearing a false sales oath after it.
rows.anchor: ويطلق العصر على الصلاة الموقتة بوقت العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the prayer reading, the article is definite by reference and the word has become a conventional name, like al-aqaba.
rows.anchor: وتعريفه على هذا تعريف العهد وصار علما بالغلبة كما هو شأن كثير من أسماء الأجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asr can mean an era identified by a generation, ruler, prophet, or religion, such as the eras of Ibrahim, Alexander, or Jahiliyya; it could here mean the Prophet's own era.
rows.anchor: ويطلق العصر على مدة معلومة لوجود جيل من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Prophet's-era reading, the article refers to the present era, like saying today; the oath resembles God's oath by the Prophet's life and by the sacred city where he is present, as Fakhr explains.
rows.anchor: ويكون المعني به عصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والتعريف فيه تعريف العهد الحضوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is the whole Islamic era, the final religious age of this world; a Prophetic parable compares Muslims, Jews, and Christians with workers hired through a day, with Muslims completing the remaining time after afternoon and receiving both groups' full wages.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد عصر الإسلام كله وهو خاتمة عصور الأديان لهذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That parable may be connected to the surah's symbolic reference to the Islamic era.
rows.anchor: فلعل ذلك التمثيل النبوي له اتصال بالرمز إلى عصر الإسلام في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asr may also mean all time; Ibn Atiyya reports Ubayy ibn Ka'b asking the Prophet about it and receiving the answer that the Lord swears by the latter part of the day.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية :  قال أبي بن كعب :  سألت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading al-asr as the Islamic era especially suits the surah, which distinguishes people in that era by disbelief or faith and by how fully they practice Islam; pre-Islamic peoples differed in access to messengers and held superseded or idolatrous religions.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة القسم بالعصر لغرض السورة على إرادة عصر الإسلام ظاهرة فإنها بينت حال الناس في عصر الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan is a generic definite with customary comprehensive force: people living when Islam appeared, especially those reached by its call across the world; after the exception of believers who do good, the judgment remains true of others.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس مراد به الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss, the opposite of profit in trade, is a metaphor for the bad afterlife outcome of someone who expects a good end, whether bliss or punishment; it echoes the cited verse about an unprofitable trade.
rows.anchor: مصدر وهو ضد الربح في التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in loss uses figurative containment: being enclosed by loss is stronger than simply calling a person a loser.
rows.anchor: شبهت ملازمة الخسر بإحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal assertion, strengthened by the oath and emphatic particle, warns of the condition enveloping most people.
rows.anchor: يفيد التهويل والإنذار بالحالة المحيطة بمعظم الناس
